title: Design: AccountingHub record of a closed internal work order
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have AccountingHub enabled.
  • Have a customer flagged as Internal customer, with one asset, and its default internal category left at General Internal.
  • Have a closed internal work order with stock parts and shop supplies, made for this test.
  • Open the attached pictures iwo-flow5-03-3b-accountinghub-closed-record.png, iwo-happy-42-41-accountinghub-closed-record.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open Accounting > Sales > Invoices.
  2. Open the closed work order's record.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The list opens.

Step 2:

  • The record shows Closed with the badge, Classification, Category, Posting date, Parts cost, Shop supplies and its journal entries.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-R1: “At Close, the hub receives the invoice event carrying the classification (Internal or No Charge), the category, the original work order and line and the original technician when set, the work order number and the asset, and keeps an invoice record with a status Closed (new in the hub), the badge, "No Charge" in place of a total, and no payment tabs.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
